apps_analyzed.name: FSWizard
apps_analyzed.pricing: Free (limited) + Pro $50 one-time ($19 mobile, free with HSMAdvisor package)
strengths: Completely free or very affordable option
Highly accurate calculations (usually within 10% of manufacturer specs)
Excellent HSM (High-Speed Machining) and chip thinning support
Simple, intuitive user interface
Fast calculations suitable for shop floor use
Responsive developer who engages with user feedback
Available on mobile and web platforms
Very high user satisfaction (4.6/5 stars on iOS)
weaknesses: Limited material database in free version (full 200+ materials in Pro)
Cannot save tools locally in some implementations
Occasionally produces different results than manufacturer data
Inconsistent with HSMAdvisor and G-Wizard results on same inputs
Limited GD&T section
Missing drill specifications (60 vs 90 degree center drills)
Assumes coolant availability (problematic for dry machining)
Less advanced tool deflection modeling than HSMAdvisor
common_concerns: Accuracy variations between calculators create confusion about which to trust
Different results when same inputs used across FSWizard/HSMAdvisor/G-Wizard
Material database gaps for specialized materials
No local tool saving capability noted by users
Mobile app had one report of battery drain issues
feature_gaps: Automatic cloud sync of tool libraries

apps_analyzed.name: G-Wizard Calculator
apps_analyzed.pricing: $80/year subscription + free 30-day trial; Lifetime license available; G-Wizard Lite (free with limitations: 2 HP for 1-year sub, 5 HP for 3-year sub)
strengths: Comprehensive tool library with custom tool storage
Large material database for common materials
Considers safety limits (torque and HP limitations)
Mature product with long track record
Can import/export CSV data
Includes manufacturer recommended data
Some users report winning $20M+ aerospace projects using it
weaknesses: Expensive annual subscription model ($80/year)
Poor material database quality (missing common materials like 304/303 stainless steel, PEEK, PTFE)
Requires Adobe AIR installation (deprecated technology, security risk)
Windows 10 Enterprise compatibility issues
Inconsistent/inaccurate calculations that 'spit out random numbers'
Dangerously high feedrate recommendations (650 IPM causing tool failure)
Calculates same deflection for conical and cylindrical micro tools incorrectly
Bad plastic recommendations that cause melting at recommended RPMs
Tapered tool calculations are 'obviously wrong'
No support for entering decimal places for taper angles
Optimize cut width function doesn't work for tapered tools
Requires internet connection every 28 days
Poor customer service - terminated user license after 3-star review
common_concerns: Inaccurate for materials and tool types beyond basics
Cost-prohibitive for hobbyists and small shops
Inconsistent results compared to other calculators and real-world testing
Technical bugs not addressed despite support tickets
Unwanted newsletter ads with poor mobile design blocking content
feature_gaps: Proper material database with common materials
Better decimal precision for tool angles

apps_analyzed.name: HSMAdvisor
apps_analyzed.pricing: $65 one-time or monthly subscription; Free version available (v1.400+); Mobile included free with desktop purchase
strengths: Most accurate feeds and speeds calculations
Advanced tool protection features (deflection limits, torque limits)
Extensive material database (200+ materials and variants)
Excellent HSM (High-Speed Machining) support
Machine-specific calculations with spindle power curves
Both HP and Torque limits exposed and configurable
Tool life estimation capabilities
Circular interpolation compensation
Advanced tool management system
Tool library sharing across multiple computers
Excellent developer support and responsiveness
Comprehensive reference materials and charts
Shows tool stress levels to prevent breakage
weaknesses: Steeper learning curve for advanced features
Documentation is primarily Imperial-centric (not metric-friendly)
Material database assumes coolant availability for aluminum (problematic for dry machining)
Complex subscription options initially confusing to users
Limited metric material naming conventions
Desktop version more powerful but requires installation
May be overkill for simple/hobbyist needs
common_concerns: Advanced features have steep learning curve
Metric users struggle with Imperial-centric documentation
Some users confused by multiple purchasing/subscription options
feature_gaps: Better metric documentation and material naming
Mobile app feature parity with desktop

apps_analyzed.name: CNC Machinist Calculator Pro
strengths: Affordable pricing
Multiple calculator tools included
Decent feature set for price
Works on multiple platforms
weaknesses: Battery drain issues reported
Limited information in app store about features
Minimal user reviews available
Less comprehensive than premium options
common_concerns: Battery drain issues when running in background
No clear documentation of what's included

apps_analyzed.name: Machinist Calc Pro 2 (Calculated Industries)
apps_analyzed.pricing: Premium app (approximately half the cost of physical handheld calculator)
strengths: Replicates trusted physical calculator functionality
Brand known for quality calculation tools
Premium positioning attracts serious users
weaknesses: Premium pricing
Limited information on modern features like cloud sync or HSM support
feature_gaps: Unclear what advantages digital version has over physical calc

universal_complaints: Manual tool and material data entry is tedious and repetitive - users want saved presets
Inconsistent results between different calculators create trust issues
Limited or poor material database coverage (especially specialized materials)
Lack of cloud/automatic sync between devices (mobile/desktop)
Offline capability limitations or unclear offline feature scope
No integration with CAM software (users manually transfer numbers)
Accuracy concerns with certain material types (plastics, exotic alloys)
Documentation gaps (metric vs imperial, advanced features)
No automatic machine profile detection or setup
universal_strengths: All provide material and tool databases
All consider multiple variables (not just SFM/RPM)
All offer reference materials and charts
Free or affordable options available for each segment
All support HSM/chip thinning to some degree
All used and trusted by professional machinists
differentiation_opportunities: Automatic cloud sync of tool libraries across devices (desktop + mobile)
Full offline-first design with optional cloud sync
Seamless CAM software integration (Fusion 360, Mastercam, etc.)
Automatic tool wear tracking and life estimation
Comparison mode showing multiple calculators' results
Guided setup wizard for new users
Material preset optimization based on shop equipment
Real-time feedback on tool stress during cutting
Integration with CNC machine data for on-machine parameter adjustment
Dry vs wet machining material presets
Automatic coolant recommendation based on material selection

market_insights.pricing_sensitivity: High - users frequently compare FSWizard (free/$50) to G-Wizard ($80/year); cost is significant barrier for adoption
market_insights.accuracy_trust: Critical - multiple forums show users testing different calculators against each other and manufacturer data; inconsistent results erode trust
market_insights.platform_preference: Mobile increasingly important - users want shop floor access but desktop power features still valued for detailed setup
market_insights.workflow_integration: Major gap - users manually transfer results to CAM software; no seamless integration with standard tools
market_insights.data_management: Significant pain point - tool library management and sync across devices is constant complaint/feature request
market_insights.competitive_positioning: Strongly technical - buyers are experienced machinists; they research thoroughly and make rational feature/cost decisions
market_insights.developer_responsiveness: Key differentiator - HSMAdvisor and FSWizard praised for developer engagement; G-Wizard criticized for ignoring support tickets
market_insights.free_vs_paid: Market segmentation - free options (FSWizard free, HSMAdvisor free v1.400+) capture hobbyists/learners; paid capture professionals/production shops

small_job_shop.primary_calculator: FSWizard or CNC Machinist Calculator Pro
small_job_shop.willingness_to_pay: Medium - willing to pay if ROI clear
